Modern estimates 15,000 (Heather) to 30,000 (Williams and Friell); mid 20,000. Role split (legions/auxilia palatina, foot archers, scholae and mounted archers) is an educated guess. Command 0.35: attacked after an 8-mile march in heat, without waiting for Gratian, underestimating the Goths; cavalry attacked without orders. Training 0.75: comitatenses field army. riverCrossing false: the Romans closed overland on the Gothic camp after an 8-mile march, no river between the armies (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Adrianople).

sides.name: Goths (Thervingi, Greuthungi) and Alans (Fritigern)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. Total 12,000-15,000 (Delbrück) to 20,000 (Williams and Friell). Thervingi infantry defending the wagon laager on a hill; the Greuthungi and Alan cavalry under Alatheus and Saphrax were foraging and arrived early in the fight to strike the Roman left (reinforcement at day 0.05). Infantry/cavalry split is an educated guess. Tribal warband host mapped to archetype-feudal-host. Morale 0.85: existential, starving refugees. Wagon laager is a field fortification, not a fortified city, so fortified=false. prepared true: the Goths fought from a wagon circle set up in advance on a hilltop, with the families and possessions inside, while the Romans arrived tired from the march (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Adrianople, citing Ammianus 31.12).

outcome.note: Gothic victory; Valens killed. Roman losses 10,000-15,000 (Heather) or 20,000 (Williams and Friell), about two thirds of the army (Ammianus). Gothic losses unknown: educated guess, grade D. Fight began in the afternoon and ended at nightfall.

Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. 14,000-15,000 combatants, up to 25,000 counting armed servants (Rogers): ~10,000 men-at-arms (most dismounted = infantry_line, 800-2,400 mounted on the wings = cavalry_heavy), 4,000-5,000 archers and crossbowmen (barely used). sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Archers fought behind sharpened stakes (field fortification; not a fortified city). Morale 0.7: sick and hungry but desperate. Training 0.75: indentured professionals. prepared true: the English deployed on chosen ground before the French attack, the archers behind pointed stakes driven into the ground at an angle against cavalry (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Agincourt).

sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. About 67,000 on the field at dawn (Chandler) with 139-157 guns; ~7,000 of Davout's III Corps (Friant's division, Bourcier's dragoons) arrived after a forced march and entered the fight at Telnitz/Sokolnitz in the early morning (reinforcement at day 0.05). Command 1.0 = rubric anchor "Napoleon 1805". prepared true: Napoleon chose and occupied the position before 2 December, fortified the Santon with 18 guns, and Davout held the Goldbach line in positions described as 'both a natural and a fortified-structural barrier' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Austerlitz).

outcome.note: French victory. Allies 27,000-36,000 (15,000-16,000 killed or wounded, 12,000-20,000 captured), 186 guns lost; mid is the midpoint. French 8,569-9,288 total incl. 573-760 captured; Roberts 8,279 killed and wounded only. Fighting about 08:00 to 16:30.

sides.name: France and Bavaria (Tallard, Marsin, Maximilian II Emanuel)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. 56,000 and 90 guns. Split derived as for the Allies. Villages of Blenheim and Oberglauheim barricaded and packed with infantry (field works, not a fortified city). Main attacks from about 13:00, Blenheim garrison surrendered about 21:00.

Polybius 80,000 foot + 6,000 horse (86,400 incl. 10,000 camp garrison, excluded here) is followed by many modern historians (e.g. Goldsworthy); lower modern estimates (~50,000) set the low end. Training 0.45: many legions newly raised in 216 BCE. riverCrossing false: the Romans had camps on both banks of the Aufidus and deployed without a contested crossing (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Cannae).

sides.name: Carthage (Hannibal)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. Polybius 40,000 foot + 10,000 horse, accepted by most modern historians; +/-10% range. Gauls, Hispanics and Libyans as line, 6,000 skirmishers, 2,000 Balearic slingers, 6,000 Hispanic/Gallic heavy horse, 4,000 Numidian light horse. Hannibal's hammer-and-anvil double envelopment is mapped to macedonian-combined-arms (closest behavioural match). Command 1.0: Hannibal. Libyans partly in captured Roman mail. prepared false: both armies deployed for an open pitched battle on the day, Hannibal anchoring his left on the Aufidus, with no works (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Cannae).

outcome.note: Carthaginian victory, double envelopment. Roman field-army losses: Livy 48,200 killed + ~4,500 captured on the field (camp captives excluded because the camp garrison is not in forces); Polybius 70,000 killed. Infobox total incl. camps 67,500-80,000. Carthaginian killed 5,700 (Polybius) to 8,000 (Livy); high includes wounded at ~1:1 (derived). Ancient figures, grade C.

Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. 10,000 cavalry (Plutarch, accepted by most modern historians): 1,000 cataphracts, 9,000 horse archers, plus ~1,000 camels carrying arrow resupply (logistics, not a combat role). Weapons 3.3: composite bow with continuous resupply, kontos. Ships 2.0: no navy. Command 0.9: Surena. Training 0.85: Surena's household retainers. Surprise: Surena concealed his strength and armor behind a screen. riverCrossing false: the Parthians attacked the Roman column in open country, no contested crossing (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Carrhae).

sides.name: Roman Republic (Crassus)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. 42,000: seven legions (34,000 nominal; 28,000 if understrength), 4,000 light infantry, 4,000 cavalry incl. Publius Crassus's 1,000 Gauls (heavy). Command 0.3: Crassus marched into open country without scouts on Ariamnes' advice. Morale 0.45: thirst, heat, Publius's death. Terrain: open semi-arid plain south of Harran (steppe class; summer heat and lack of water were decisive). prepared false: Crassus's army was attacked while marching through the Mesopotamian desert and fought where it was caught (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Carrhae).

outcome.note: Parthian victory. Roman losses 20,000 killed + 10,000 captured (Plutarch, accepted in broad terms by moderns), 5,000-10,000 escaped; a large share fell during the night retreat to Carrhae and the following 1-2 days (Crassus killed at a parley), hence high duration 3. Parthian losses unknown but minimal: educated guess, grade D. Exact battlefield unknown; location is south of Harran with a wide radius.

Surprise: Operation Bertram deception concealed timing and main effort. riverCrossing false: the attack went through minefields in open desert, no river (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Battle_of_El_Alamein).

sides.name: German-Italian Panzer Army Africa
sides.note: Strength (Wikipedia infobox): 116,000 men (~50,000 German, ~66,000 Italian), 547 tanks (German ~249 incl. ~30 Pz IV Special, Italian ~280-298 M13/M14), 192 armoured cars, 552 guns, 496-1,063 anti-tank guns (not counted), 770-900 aircraft (many unserviceable). infantry_line ~40-50% of strength (164th, 90th Light, Ramcke, Folgore, Bologna, Brescia, Pavia, Trento), educated. Ratings: command 0.6 (Stumme died 24 Oct, Rommel back 25 Oct, mixed German-Italian command); morale 0.5; training 0.6 (Afrika Korps veterans, weaker Italian infantry). prepared true: Rommel had time to fortify the line, sowing about 500,000 mines and miles of barbed wire (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Battle_of_El_Alamein, citing Bierman and Smith 2003 p.255).

outcome.note: 23 Oct - 4 Nov 1942 (Operations Lightfoot and Supercharge; Axis withdrawal ordered 4 Nov). Eighth Army 13,560 casualties (infobox), 332-500 tanks knocked out (many repaired). Axis 41,800-73,000 casualties incl. ~30,000 prisoners; ~500 tanks destroyed. Mid is the centre of the published range, not a measured value.

name: Falklands War: land campaign (San Carlos to Stanley)

sides.name: United Kingdom (3 Commando Brigade, 5 Infantry Brigade, Task Force)
sides.note: Strength: 4,000 men of 3 Commando Brigade landed at San Carlos on 21 May (40, 42, 45 Cdo; 2 and 3 Para), 5 Infantry Brigade (2 Scots Guards, 1 Welsh Guards, 1/7 Gurkha Rifles) added ~5,000 by 1 June (Wikipedia); infantry_line counts rifle strength, educated (~600-700 per battalion plus SAS/SBS). Armour: 4 Scorpion + 4 Scimitar (Blues and Royals). Artillery: 29 Cdo Regt three batteries + 29 Bty 4 Fd Regt, 105 mm Light Guns in 6-gun batteries: 18 + 12 = 30 (DTIC ADA401278); low = guns ashore in the first days. Air: 28 Sea Harrier FRS1 (fighter), ~10-14 Harrier GR3 (strike); helicopters ~100 (Sea King, Wessex, Gazelle, Scout, one Chinook), educated. Naval: 2 carriers, 2 LPDs, ~23 destroyers/frigates; 5 SSN + 1 SSK, educated from the Task Force list. Tech (derived:tech-anchor, 1982 near 1985 anchor 9): weapons 8.8 (Milan, AIM-9L, Rapier, Sea Dart); armor 8.4 (only light CVR(T)); comms 8.8 (SCOT satcom). Ratings: training 0.95 = elite long-service professionals (Paras, Royal Marines, Guards, Gurkhas); command 0.8; morale 0.8. riverCrossing false: the advance from San Carlos to Stanley was overland across East Falkland (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falklands_War). objective kind capture: the land campaign from San Carlos aimed at Stanley, taken with the Argentine surrender on 14 June, the last day of this window (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falklands_War).

sides.name: Argentina (Malvinas garrison and air forces)
sides.note: Strength: ~13,000 land forces at peak on the islands (Wikipedia infobox), incl. air force and support personnel; infantry_line = ~8-10 army infantry regiments plus BIM 5 marines, educated. ifv_apc = 12 Panhard AML-90 armoured cars. Artillery: ~30 OTO Melara 105 mm pack howitzers (1.5 battalions, British estimate in DTIC ADA401278) plus a few 155 mm. Aircraft were mainland-based at the edge of their radius: Mirage III/Dagger as fighters; A-4 Skyhawk, Super Etendard, Canberra, Pucara (on the islands), MB-339 as strike; counts educated. Fleet stayed in port after the Belgrano sinking (2 May), so no ships are listed. Starts: Stanley and its mountain ring (Longdon, Two Sisters, Tumbledown, Wireless Ridge), outer Mount Kent area, Goose Green/Darwin, Port Howard and Fox Bay on West Falkland. Tech: logistics 7.5 (air bridge, then blockade; troops underfed). Ratings: command 0.35 (Menendez static, poor army/air coordination); morale 0.4 (cold, hungry conscripts; BIM 5 an exception); training 0.4 (1963-class conscripts with months of service). Fortified: prepared positions on the high ground. prepared true: the final British attacks of 11-14 June were made against the heavily defended ring of high ground surrounding Stanley, garrisoned since April (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falklands_War). objective kind hold: Argentina held Stanley from 2 April and sought to keep it until the surrender on 14 June (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falklands_War).

outcome.note: 21 May (San Carlos) to 14 June 1982 (surrender at Stanley). Argentina: 11,313 captured over the war (Wikipedia), of whom the vast majority on the islands, plus land-campaign killed (~250-300 of the 649 total; 323 died on the Belgrano) and ~1,000 wounded, educated split. UK: war total 255 killed, 775 wounded, 115 captured; land-campaign share incl. Sir Galahad (48 killed, 115 wounded) but excluding ship losses at sea is an educated range. Goose Green alone: 961 Argentines captured. Grade C on losses.

name: Battle of France (Fall Gelb and Fall Rot)

sides.name: Germany
sides.note: Strength (Wikipedia infobox citing Umbreit, David, Hooton; Frieser 2005 pp.35-37): ~3.0-3.3 million men in 135-141 divisions, 2,439 (Frieser) / 2,445 (Umbreit) tanks, 7,378 guns, 5,638 aircraft incl. gliders and transports. infantry_line: ~141 divisions x ~9,500 riflemen/pioneers, excluding crews, artillery, signals and trains (educated split of the 3.3M total). cavalry_light: 1st Cavalry Division. Aircraft: 836 Bf 109 (Hooton) + ~250 Bf 110 = fighters; Luftflotten II and III had 1,771 + 1,756 front-line aircraft, remainder after fighters = bombers, Stukas, recon (split is derived, not quoted). Italian Alpine front (22 divisions) excluded: outside bbox. Starts: Army Group B (Lower Rhine), Army Group A (Eifel, incl. Panzergruppe Kleist and most OKH reserves), Army Group C (Saar). Tech (derived:tech-anchor, 1940 between anchors 7 and 8): communications 8 = radio in every tank and command vehicle; air 8 = Bf 109E/Ju 87 near the 1943 anchor; logistics 7.5 = rail plus horse-drawn infantry divisions, motorised only in mobile divisions. Ratings: command 0.85 = trained General Staff, Manstein plan, Guderian; training 0.7; morale 0.7 after Poland. Surprise: Ardennes main effort was not expected by the Allies. riverCrossing true: the decisive breakthrough required assault crossings of the Meuse (Sedan, Dinant) on 13 May before Guderian and Rommel broke out of the Meuse bridgeheads (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_France). objective kind capture: Germany set out to defeat France and took Paris on 14 June (day 35 of this 43-day window to the 22 June armistice) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_France).

sides.name: Allies (France, Britain, Belgium, Netherlands)
sides.note: Strength (Wikipedia citing Frieser 2005 pp.36-37): 104 French divisions for the north, 13 BEF, 22 Belgian, 10 Dutch, 2 Polish; ~3.3 million men; guns: France 10,700 + Britain 1,280 + Belgium 1,338 + Dutch 656 = ~14,000 (13,974 infobox). Tanks: French 3,254 on the north-east front (Frieser) to 4,071 (Zaloga, all French), plus ~310 British; Belgian/Dutch armour negligible. Fighters: 81 Belgian + 261 British + 764 French = 1,106 in theatre (Hooton); high adds RAF Fighter Command sorties from England. Strike: Armee de l'Air 1,562 aircraft total, AASF and Bomber Command ~392, minus fighters (derived range). infantry_line: ~150 divisions x ~8,500 riflemen, educated split. cavalry_light: horse elements of the DLC/brigades, educated. Starts: Dutch Fortress Holland, Belgian KW/Albert Canal line, French 1st Army Group + BEF on the Belgian border (Dyle plan), Sedan-Meuse (9th/2nd Armies), Maginot Line (2nd/3rd Army Groups), GQG reserve. Tech: fortification 8 = Maginot Line is the anchor (fortified flag left false because most of the field army was not in it); armor 7.8 (Char B1, Somua S35 thicker than German tanks); communications 7.1 (most tanks without radio, GQG without radio links). Ratings: command 0.4 (Gamelin's slow chain of command, Dyle-Breda overcommitment); morale 0.5; training 0.55 (many B-series reserve divisions). prepared false at campaign level: under the Dyle plan the main Franco-British mobile forces advanced into Belgium on 10 May to a line they had to reach before the Germans, and later lines were improvised; only static sectors such as the Maginot Line were prepared in advance (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_France). objective kind hold: the Allies controlled Paris at the start and sought to keep it; it was declared open and fell on 14 June (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_France).

outcome.note: 10 May - 25 June 1940 (46 days); Paris fell 14 June (day 35), armistice signed 22 June (day 43). German losses 27,074 killed, 111,034 wounded, 18,384 missing = 156,547 (Frieser 1995 p.400); high adds ~6,000 Italian losses on the Alpine front. Allied losses ~73,000 killed, 240,000 wounded, 15,000 missing, 1,756,000 captured = 2,084,000 (infobox); French SHD: 85,310 killed, 120,000 wounded, 1,540,000 prisoners; range covers both counts.

sides.name: Achaemenid Empire (Darius III)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. Command 0.4: Darius fled; coordination of satrapal contingents poor. prepared false: Darius waited on ground cleared and levelled for his scythed chariots, an offensive preparation without defensive works, and opened with chariot and cavalry attacks (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Gaugamela).

outcome.note: Macedonian victory. Ancient Macedonian dead 1,100-1,500 (Arrian/Curtius/Diodorus), wounded not reported; mid 3,000 assumes ~1.5 wounded per killed (derived). Persian dead 40,000 (Curtius) to 90,000 (Diodorus), Arrian claims 300,000 captured (absurd). Mid 35,000 is an educated guess (~1/3 of mid strength), grade C.

Army 65,000-75,000 (possibly 80,000), 270 guns, ~9,500 cavalry overall. Day 0 (1 July) = divisions of Heth, Pender, Rodes and Early, ~27,000 engaged (Livermore via Martin). Arrivals: day 0.3 (evening 1 July) Anderson and Johnson; day 1.0 (morning 2 July) Hood and McLaws of Longstreet's corps; day 1.5 Stuart's three cavalry brigades (no role on 2 July); day 1.8 Pickett's division (fought 3 July). Divisional strengths and per-arrival gun counts follow Busey & Martin as commonly cited (approximate, not fetched). Weapons 6.5: rifled muskets, mixed rifled/smoothbore artillery. Morale 0.9 after Chancellorsville. riverCrossing false: the Confederates attacked overland from Seminary Ridge and the town (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Gettysburg).

sides.name: United States: Army of the Potomac (Meade)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. Comms 6.7: telegraph and signal corps. Fortification 6.6: breastworks on Culp's Hill and the fish-hook ridge line (field works, not a fortified city). prepared true for days 2-3, which carry most of the fighting: the Union held the fishhook line on Cemetery Ridge and Culp's Hill, partly behind newly built breastworks; day 1 was a meeting engagement (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Gettysburg).

outcome.note: Union victory. Union 23,049 (3,155 killed, 14,529 wounded, 5,365 captured or missing). Confederate 23,000-28,000 (Busey & Martin 23,231; higher totals count stragglers captured in the retreat). Day 1 alone: Union ~9,000, Confederate ~6,000. From ~07:30 on 1 July to the end of Pickett's Charge ~16:00 on 3 July (2.4 days); Lee withdrew on 4 July.

name: Gulf War ground campaign (Operation Desert Sabre)

sides.name: Coalition (US, UK, France, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Syria, Gulf states)
sides.note: Strength: >540,000 coalition troops from 31 countries in theatre, 1,736 combat aircraft (Conduct of the Persian Gulf War, DoD 1992). VII Corps >142,000 soldiers with 1,587 tanks, 1,502 Bradleys/APCs, 669 artillery pieces, 223 attack helicopters; XVIII Corps 116,000 (Whirlwind War, CMH); XVIII Corps alone >1,000 helicopters (Certain Victory). Coalition totals: 3,113 tanks, 2,200 artillery systems (Wikipedia infobox); high adds Arab, USMC and reserve tanks. infantry_line = dismounted infantry of ~17 division-equivalents (~20-30% of ground strength), educated. ifv_apc and the fighter/strike split of the 1,736 combat aircraft are educated. Starts: XVIII Corps near Rafha (far west), VII Corps west of Wadi al-Batin, Joint Forces Command North, I MEF, Joint Forces Command East on the coast. Tech (derived:tech-anchor): 1991 just above the 1985 anchor 9: M1A1 with thermal sights, GPS, JSTARS, F-117 and laser-guided bombs; cyber 9 = 1990 networks anchor. Ratings: command 0.85 (CENTCOM joint planning, left hook); morale 0.75; training 0.85 (US volunteer force trained at the NTC; Arab partners lower). Surprise: the western envelopment was not detected. riverCrossing false: the ground offensive went through berms and minefields in open desert, no river (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_War). objective kind capture: the coalition aim was the liberation of Kuwait, Kuwaiti forces liberated the city during the 100-hour ground war (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_War).

sides.name: Iraq (forces in the Kuwait Theater of Operations)
sides.note: Strength at G-day (24 Feb): DIA credited 540,000-545,000 troops, 43 divisions, 4,280 tanks, 2,800 APCs, 3,100 guns (CPGW); the Gulf War Air Power Survey revised this to no more than 336,000 on 17 Jan, then 25-30% desertion and <10% air casualties leaving ~200,000-222,000 by 24 Feb; equipment ~800 fewer tanks and 600 fewer guns than DIA thought, then air attrition (CENTCOM: 39% tanks, 32% APCs, 47% artillery; CIA/DIA lower). Counts above apply those decrements (derived, grade C). infantry_line ~65-75% of the 200,000-222,000, educated. Air force did not fight (hid or fled to Iran), so no aircraft are listed. Starts: frontline infantry divisions on the Saudi border, tactical armoured reserves (12th, 52nd, 17th, 10th Armd), coast and Kuwait City, western flank (26th, 45th Divs near As Salman), Republican Guard on the Kuwait-Iraq border. Tech: T-72M/T-62/T-55/Type 69, 1970s Soviet kit; ISR 7 (no air reconnaissance in the war); cyber 7 = computerised KARI air-defence network but no network warfare (educated, outside the anchor table). Ratings: command 0.25 (centralised, frozen); morale 0.2 (deserting, short of food and water after 38 days of bombing); training 0.4 (Republican Guard higher). Fortified: Saddam Line berms, minefields, fire trenches. prepared true: coalition breaching forces cleared fortified trench systems, bunkers and minefields built during the months of occupation (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_War). objective kind hold: Iraq occupied Kuwait City from August 1990 and was ordered to hold Kuwait (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_War).

outcome.note: 24-28 Feb 1991, 100 hours. Iraq: ~86,000 prisoners (64,000 taken by US forces; CPGW) plus ground-war killed and wounded; whole-war Iraqi military dead 20,000-50,000 (Wikipedia), of which an uncertain share fell in the ground war; range is an educated composite. CENTCOM credited 3,847 tanks, 1,450 APCs and 2,917 artillery destroyed or captured over the whole campaign; GWAPS: 76% tank attrition by war's end. Coalition: whole war 292 killed (147 hostile), 776 wounded (467 in action) (Wikipedia); ground-war share incl. Arab partners is educated. Grade C on losses.

sides.name: Normandy (William)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. Composition about 1/2 infantry, 1/4 cavalry, 1/4 archers and crossbowmen. Contemporary 14,000-150,000 rejected. Command 0.8: William; feigned retreats used. riverCrossing false: the Normans attacked uphill across open ground, no river (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Hastings).

sides.name: England (Harold Godwinson)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. Modern estimates 5,000-13,000; almost all infantry, few archers. Housecarls and thegns as infantry_line, poorly equipped fyrd as infantry_light (split is an educated guess). Shield wall on Senlac ridge. Morale 0.65 and training 0.55: tired after Stamford Bridge (25 Sept) and the march south; elite housecarls mixed with fyrd. prepared false: Harold had tried to surprise William, was forestalled when William marched first, and took a defensive position on Senlac Hill on the morning of the battle after a forced march, without field works (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Hastings).

outcome.note: Norman victory; Harold killed. Fighting from about 9 am to dusk (sunset 16:54). Casualties unknown: Marren speculates ~2,000 Norman and ~4,000 English dead; ~50% English fatality rate among known participants. Wounded added by educated guess.

name: 2003 invasion of Iraq (Operation Iraqi Freedom, major combat)

sides.name: Coalition (US, UK, Australia, Poland)
sides.note: Strength: 589,799 coalition personnel total incl. naval/air and 70,000 Peshmerga (Wikipedia infobox); ~250,000 soldiers massed on the Kuwait border (On Point); 1,800 coalition aircraft (On Point); 101st Airborne alone self-deployed >250 helicopters (On Point). Ground manoeuvre: 3rd Infantry Division, 101st Airborne, 82nd Airborne elements, 1st Marine Division, Task Force Tarawa, UK 1st Armoured Division, 3 Commando and 16 Air Assault Brigades. infantry_line (dismounts), armour, ifv_apc, artillery and helicopter counts are educated reconstructions from that order of battle (no fetched source gives the totals; grade D for these). Fighter/strike split of the 1,800 aircraft (which include tankers and support) educated. Kurdish Peshmerga and northern SOF are outside the theatre and excluded. Reinforcement day 23: 4th Infantry Division entering from Kuwait mid-April, educated. Starts: V Corps in western Kuwait, I MEF and UK in eastern Kuwait, SOF in the western desert. Doctrine us-joint-2026 is the closest available id (networked joint precision warfare), not a claim of 2026 capability. Tech (derived:tech-anchor, 2003 between 9 and 10): JDAM, Javelin, Blue Force Tracker, Predator. Ratings: command 0.85; morale 0.75; training 0.9 (long-service volunteers). Surprise: G-day preceded the air campaign (On Point). riverCrossing true: the advance had to seize contested Euphrates bridges, with heavy fighting for two major bridges in Nasiriyah and Iraqi troops defending key Euphrates bridges near Karbala (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_invasion_of_Iraq). objective kind capture: the invasion aimed at Baghdad, taken on 9 April, day 21 of this window (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_invasion_of_Iraq).

sides.name: Iraq (Regular Army, Republican Guard, Fedayeen Saddam)
sides.note: Strength: Army 280,000-350,000 in 17 divisions, Republican Guard 50,000-80,000, >2,200 tanks, 2,400 APCs, 4,000 artillery pieces (On Point Figure 45); IISS: ground forces 350,000, Fedayeen Saddam 44,000; other estimate Fedayeen 20,000-40,000 (Wikipedia). infantry_line excludes crews and the northern corps facing the Kurds only partly (educated ~65-75% of army + RG); infantry_light = Fedayeen and Ba'ath militia. Air force did not fly, so no aircraft listed. Starts: III Corps at Basra, 11th Division at Nasiriyah, IV Corps at Amarah, RG Baghdad Division at Kut, Medina/Nebuchadnezzar at Karbala-Hillah, Baghdad, militia at Najaf/Samawah, Tikrit. Tech: 1970s-80s Soviet kit degraded by sanctions; ISR 7 (no air reconnaissance); cyber 7 educated (outside the anchor table). Ratings: command 0.2 (Saddam's interference, RG mispositioned); morale 0.3 (regular army melted away; Fedayeen fanatical); training 0.35. Not fortified: no prepared defence of Baghdad. prepared true: Iraqi forces were deployed in advance, entrenched in and around Tallil airfield and with two Republican Guard divisions positioned to block the Karbala Gap (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_invasion_of_Iraq). objective kind hold: the regime controlled Baghdad and sought to hold it (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_invasion_of_Iraq).

outcome.note: 20 March - 9 April 2003 (Baghdad, day 21); Tikrit taken 15 April (day 27). Coalition: 172 killed (139 US, 33 UK), 551 US wounded, Peshmerga 24+ killed (Wikipedia), a handful captured. Iraq: combatant fatalities 7,600-10,800, best estimate ~9,200 (Project on Defense Alternatives); Wikipedia range 11,000-45,000; >7,300 EPWs in coalition custody on 9 April (On Point); wounded unknown (educated ~1.5-2.5x killed). Many soldiers simply went home and are not counted as losses. Grade C on losses.

sides.name: Germany (9th Army, 4th Panzer Army, Army Detachment Kempf)
sides.note: Strength (Wikipedia infobox citing Frieser and Zetterling/Frankson): 780,900 men, 2,928 tanks and assault guns (low ~2,450 = tanks only), 9,966 guns and mortars (low excludes light mortars, educated), 2,110 aircraft. infantry_line ~45-50% of strength across ~50 divisions (17 panzer/panzergrenadier), educated split. Fighter/strike split of Luftflotte 4 and 6 is educated. Tech (derived:tech-anchor, 1943 = anchor 8): weapons/armor 8.1-8.2 (Tiger, Panther, Ferdinand debut); logistics 7.6 (horse-drawn infantry divisions, rail-fed). Ratings: command 0.75 (trained staff, Manstein/Model, but a delayed and predictable offensive); morale 0.65; training 0.7. No surprise: the Soviets knew the plan and timing. riverCrossing false: only Army Detachment Kempf had to cross the Northern Donets against the dug-in 7th Guards Army; 9th Army and 4th Panzer Army attacked overland (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Kursk).

sides.name: Soviet Union (Central and Voronezh Fronts; Steppe Front as reinforcement)
sides.note: Strength (Wikipedia citing Glantz/House, Zetterling/Frankson, Healy): Central Front 711,575 men (510,983 combat), Voronezh Front 625,591 (446,236 combat); together ~1,300,000 men, 3,600 tanks (1,061 light T-60/T-70), ~20,000 guns and mortars, 2,792 aircraft (Bergstrom). infantry_line ~55-65% of the 957,219 'combat soldiers' plus rifle troops counted elsewhere, educated. Reinforcement day 6 (11-12 July): Steppe Front had 573,195 men (449,133 combat) and ~1,600 tanks in reserve; 5th Guards Tank Army (~650-850 tanks) and 5th Guards Army were committed at Prokhorovka; mid assumes about half the front engaged, high = all of it (Steppe Front's 70,085 casualties in the defensive operation show heavy commitment). Tech: fortification 8.3 (eight defensive belts, e.g. 6th Guards Army: 69,688 AT + 64,430 AP mines in its first belt alone); ISR 7.9 (strategic warning of timing and axes). Ratings: command 0.75 (Zhukov, Vasilevsky, Rokossovsky, Vatutin; proven staff system by 1943); morale 0.8 after Stalingrad; training 0.55. prepared true: the Central and Voronezh Fronts each built three main defensive belts while the offensive was delayed (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Kursk, citing Glantz and House 2004 pp.64-67).

outcome.note: Citadel 5-16 July 1943 (northern face stalled by 14 July; Soviet defensive operation officially 5-23 July). German: 54,182 casualties during Citadel (Frieser, from German archive records); high allows later counts to 23 July. Soviet: 177,847 for the Kursk defensive operation (Krivosheev: Central 33,897, Voronezh 73,892, Steppe 70,085); high allows for later authors who judge Krivosheev low (unfetched, educated margin). Material: German 252-323 AFVs destroyed; Soviet 1,614-1,956 tanks/SPGs destroyed.

sides.name: Athens and Plataea
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. Hoplites 10,000-11,000 incl. ~600-1,000 Plataeans (modern estimates, Wikipedia infobox). Light troops / armed slaves possibly present but unquantified, omitted. Weapons/armor between anchors 2 (1400 BCE) and 3 (300 BCE): bronze panoply, aspis, dory. Command 0.65: Miltiades, competent (rubric 0.5-0.75). Morale 0.9: existential defence of Athens. Training 0.4: citizen militia between levy (0.25) and conscript (0.5). riverCrossing false: the Athenians advanced across the open plain, no contested crossing (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Marathon).

sides.name: Achaemenid expeditionary force (Datis, Artaphernes)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. Modern consensus ~25,000 infantry (range 20,000-100,000 in the literature; low end set to 15,000 because part may have re-embarked). Ancient totals 100,000-600,000 (Nepos, Plutarch, Plato) rejected. Split ~1/3 spearmen, 2/3 archers is an educated guess from the sparabara spear-and-bow formation. ~1,000 cavalry unengaged per most modern readings, so mid 0. Lighter armor (linen/scale, wicker shields) than hoplites, armor 2.4. Comms/logistics 2.9: depot and relay-post system. Training 0.6: professional Persian/Saka core plus subject levies. prepared false: the Persians were drawn up on the open plain without works and were surprised by the Athenian advance at a run (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Marathon).

outcome.note: Athenian victory. Herodotus gives 192 Athenian dead (generally accepted: burial mound); wounded unknown, mid 500 is an educated guess. Persian dead 6,400 per Herodotus; other modern estimates 1,000-2,000; mid 5,000 placed between them (derived, grade C), 7 ships taken. Duration: "a long time" (Herodotus), a few hours. Date disputed (August or 12 September 490 BCE), dry season either way.

sides.name: Mongol Empire (Batu, Subutai)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. Estimates 15,000-30,000 (Wikipedia infobox), others 20,000/50,000/70,000; Rashid al-Din gives 40,000 for the whole central-European invasion, only part at Mohi. Mid 25,000, high 50,000 (70,000 treated as outlier). 40/60 lancer/horse-archer split is an educated guess. At least seven stone throwers cleared the Sajo bridge. Initial force = Batu's bridge column (~60%); Subutai's column crossed downstream and hit the Hungarian flank/camp later in the morning (reinforcement at day 0.1, split is an educated guess). Command 1.0 = rubric anchor "Mongols 1241". Comms 4.2 / ISR 4.3: yam relay, flag signals, wide scouting. riverCrossing true: the Mongols had to force the Sajo, using seven stone throwers against the crossbowmen holding the bridge while Sejban crossed at a ford and Subutai built an emergency bridge to the south (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Mohi).

sides.name: Kingdom of Hungary (Bela IV)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. Estimates 25,000/50,000/80,000 (infobox); the near-contemporary Epternacher Notiz reports 10,000 Hungarian dead, suggesting an army near that size, so low 10,000, mid 25,000, high 50,000 (80,000 outlier). Role split is an educated guess. Cuman auxiliaries had left after Koten's murder. Camped in a wagon fort (field fortification, not a fortified city). Command 0.3: king at odds with barons, poor reconnaissance. Morale 0.4. prepared false: the main army sat in its fortified wagon camp and did not believe a full-scale attack was coming; only a detachment held the bridge, and the camp was then surrounded (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Mohi).

outcome.note: Mongol victory. A near-contemporary source reports 10,000 Hungarian dead, "almost the entire army"; many more cut down in the pursuit toward Pest. Mongol losses: modern estimates several hundred to several thousand. Dawn attack across the Sajo, camp broken by about midday. Forces and losses are the weakest-documented in this set.

sides.name: Israel (Southern Command)
sides.note: Strength: 70,000 men and 800 tanks in the Sinai campaign (Dupuy, Elusive Victory pp.240-244, tabulated in DTIC ADA325045 Table A-2); three divisions of ~15,000 men and ~300 tanks each (Herzog via DTIC ADA393361). infantry_line = 70,000 minus tank crews, gunners and support, educated. Half-tracks (ifv_apc) and artillery are educated guesses (Sharon alone massed ~90 guns at Abu Ageila, Wikipedia/Oren). Aircraft: IAF ~250-275 combat aircraft (Oren; Gawrych), nearly all used against Egypt on 5 June: Mirage IIICJ/Super Mystere as fighters, Mystere IV/Ouragan/Vautour/Fouga as strike, educated split. Starts: Tal (Rafah/Khan Yunis), Yoffe (between), Sharon (Nitzana, vs Abu Ageila), southern feint from Eilat/Kuntilla. Tech (derived:tech-anchor, 1967 between 8 and 9): communications 8.5 (radio down to tank level, mission orders); air 8.6 (Mirage III). Ratings: command 0.85 (Tal, Sharon, Yoffe; combined-arms flanking plan); morale 0.85 (perceived existential threat); training 0.75 (reservist army with long annual training). Surprise: Operation Focus destroyed the Egyptian air force on the ground in the first hours. riverCrossing false: the Sinai advance was overland and stopped on the canal, which was not crossed (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-Day_War). objective kind capture: Israeli units drove to and stopped along the Suez Canal before the 9 June ceasefire, inside this window (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-Day_War).

sides.name: Egypt (Sinai Field Army)
sides.note: Strength: ~100,000 of Egypt's 160,000 troops in the Sinai in seven divisions plus independent brigades, 900-950 tanks, 1,100 APCs, >1,000 guns (Pollack 2004 p.59 via Wikipedia); Dupuy: 100,000 men, 930 tanks (DTIC ADA325045); DTIC ADA393361: ~100,000 soldiers, 1,000 tanks. infantry_line ~70% of the 100,000, educated. Aircraft: 419-420 combat aircraft (Morris, Oren): MiG-21/19/17 as fighters, Su-7, Il-28, Tu-16 as strike (educated split); ~300 destroyed on 5 June. Starts: Rafah/Gaza (7th Inf Div, 20th Palestinian Div), El Arish, Abu Ageila-Umm Katef (2nd Inf Div), Kusseima, Jebel Libni/Bir Hasana (armoured reserve), Shazly Force near Kuntilla/Nakhl, Bir Gifgafa. Tech: T-54/55, IS-3, SU-100, MiG-21 (Soviet early-1960s kit, near Israeli level); fortification 8 = Abu Ageila and Rafah defended localities in depth. Ratings: command 0.25 ('ad hoc': Amer ordered a general withdrawal after Abu Ageila fell on 6 June); morale 0.45; training 0.45 (one third reservists, one third Yemen veterans). prepared true: Egypt had constructed fortified defences in the Sinai, e.g. the heavily fortified Um-Katef area at Abu-Ageila (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-Day_War). objective kind hold: Egypt held El Arish and the Sinai defences at the start; Israeli forces took the city on 5-6 June (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-Day_War).

outcome.note: 5 June 0815 - ceasefire 9 June 0435 on the Sinai front. Israel (Sinai): 275 killed and 61 tanks lost (DTIC ADA393361 citing Herzog); war total 776-983 killed, 4,517 wounded; Sinai wounded share is an educated estimate (~800-1,500). Egypt: 9,800-15,000 killed or missing (El Gamasy; Herzog), 4,338 captured, wounded unknown (educated 2,000-15,000); DTIC ADA393361 gives 12,000 men and 700 tanks lost. Grade C on losses.

name: Stalingrad strategic offensive (Operations Uranus, Little Saturn, Ring)

sides.name: Soviet Union (Southwestern, Don and Stalingrad Fronts)
sides.note: Strength (Wikipedia Stalingrad and Uranus infoboxes; Krivosheev): 1,103,000-1,143,500 personnel incl. reserves, 804-979 tanks (894 infobox), 13,400-13,451 guns and mortars, 1,000-1,500 aircraft (1,115 infobox). infantry_line ~55% of personnel (rifle troops, excluding crews, gunners, rear services), educated split; cavalry_light = 3rd Guards, 4th and 8th Cavalry Corps (~8 divisions), educated. artillery low excludes light mortars. Fighter/strike split of the air armies is an educated ~50/50. Totals already include the 2nd Guards Army committed in December, so no separate reinforcement. Starts: Serafimovich/Kletskaya bridgeheads (5th Tank, 21st Army), Don Front (65th, 24th, 66th), 62nd Army in the city, 57th/51st Armies south of Stalingrad, Southwestern Front left wing on the Middle Don (Little Saturn). Tech (derived:tech-anchor, 1942 just below the 1943 anchor): armor 7.9 (T-34/76, KV-1), logistics 7.4 (rail to the Don, few trucks), communications 7.5 (radio scarce below brigade). Ratings: command 0.7 (Vasilevsky/Zhukov staff planning, Vatutin, Rokossovsky, Yeremenko; still uneven execution); morale 0.8 existential defence; training 0.5. Surprise: Uranus achieved operational surprise against the Romanian flanks. riverCrossing false: the Soviets attacked from bridgeheads they had kept on the right bank of the Don and from positions south of the city, not by a contested crossing (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Stalingrad). objective changed from Kalach-na-Donu (link-up achieved by late 22 November, day 4) to the 6th Army pocket in Stalingrad, because this 19 Nov-2 Feb window ends with Operation Koltso, which forced the capitulation of the forces encircled in the city after Paulus's headquarters in the Univermag department store gave up (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Koltso; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Uranus); point = Square of the Fallen Fighters beside the Univermag, 48.708 N 44.516 E (https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?q=%D0%9F%D0%BB%D0%BE%D1%89%D0%B0%D0%B4%D1%8C+%D0%9F%D0%B0%D0%B2%D1%88%D0%B8%D1%85+%D0%91%D0%BE%D1%80%D1%86%D0%BE%D0%B2%2C+%D0%92%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%B3%D0%BE%D0%B3%D1%80%D0%B0%D0%B4). objective kind destroy, radiusKm 50: the Soviet aim was the encircled force, not ground. After the link-up the Red Army strengthened the outer ring 'with the intention of destroying the encircled German units', 250,000-300,000 Axis soldiers in a pocket 50 km east to west and 40 km north to south (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Uranus, Aftermath); the window ends when Koltso forced the capitulation of that force (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Koltso). The Univermag point lies on the Volga at the pocket's eastern edge, so the 50 km east-west extent is the radius that reaches its western edge (Pitomnik, Marinovka); before: kind capture of the Univermag, which counted ground and not the surrender.

sides.name: Axis (German 6th Army and 4th Panzer Army, Romanian 3rd and 4th Armies, Italian 8th Army)
sides.note: Strength (Wikipedia Stalingrad infobox, counter-offensive phase): 1,011,000 personnel, 640+ tanks, 732 aircraft (402 serviceable); Uranus infobox: Germans 400,000 in 6th Army and 4th Panzer Army, Romanians 143,296-200,000 with 827 guns and 134 tanks. infantry_line ~50% of personnel, educated split. Artillery: ~2,000 guns and mortars trapped in the pocket (Uranus article) plus Romanian 827 and Italian/4th Pz Army pieces; total is an educated guess (grade D). Aircraft split of the 732 is educated. Reinforcement day 23 (12 Dec) = LVII Panzer Corps for Operation Winter Storm (6th Panzer Division ~160 tanks + 23rd Panzer), educated range. Tech: blend of German (weapons 8, air 8) and weaker Romanian/Italian formations (anti-tank weapons inadequate vs T-34); logistics 7.2 = single rail line, overextended. Ratings: command 0.6 (Hitler's hold order, Paulus passive; staff competent); morale 0.5 falling to near collapse in the pocket; training 0.55 averaged German and allied. Not fortified: the city was ruins, the Don flanks thinly held by Romanians. prepared true: the Axis had held static positions on the Don and in the city since the autumn, with minefields in front of the Romanian lines, though thinly spread (Third Romanian Army on 140 km) and short of anti-tank guns (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Uranus). objective kind hold: Hitler ordered 6th Army to stay in Stalingrad rather than break out; it capitulated on 2 February 1943, the last day of this window (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Stalingrad; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Uranus).

outcome.note: 19 Nov 1942 (Uranus) to 2 Feb 1943 (surrender of the northern pocket). Soviet: Krivosheev offensive phase 154,885 irrecoverable (ru-wiki citing Krivosheev) plus ~330,892 sanitary (Krivosheev 1997 table; = 650,878 battle total sanitary minus defensive phase) = 485,777; high allows Pereslegin-style upward revisions. Axis: 250,000-330,000 encircled; Ziemke: 'somewhat over 200,000' lost in the pocket, 30,000 wounded flown out, Soviet figure 147,000 killed and wounded + 91,000 captured; Romanian losses 109,000-158,854 (incl. 70,000 captured, Nov-Dec), Italian 8th Army 114,520 (part falls in Little Saturn, Dec). Range: low = pocket + Romanians only; high = Wilson's 800,000 incl. Romanians.

sides.name: German 8th Army
sides.note: Strength: 150,000 men committed, 728 guns and howitzers, 294 MGs (Hastings 2013 p.281 via Wikipedia infobox). infantry_line = 150,000 minus artillery crews, cavalry, staff and trains (~20-25%), educated split. Divisional cavalry only; 1st Cavalry Division screened Rennenkampf. Tech (derived:tech-anchor): weapons 7 = 1905 anchor (magazine rifle, MG, QF artillery); armor 6.5 (no steel helmet yet, below the 1915 part of anchor 7); logistics 7.2 (interior railways moved I Corps and XVII Corps to the flanks); ISR 7.2 (aerial reconnaissance located Russian columns) plus uncoded Russian radio intercepts; cyber 0 absent-in-era. Ratings (derived:rating-rubric): command 0.8 = trained staff system, proven commanders (Hindenburg, Ludendorff, Hoffmann, Francois); morale 0.7 defending homeland territory; training 0.65 conscripts + reservists of a long-service cadre army. riverCrossing false: the envelopment was fought overland in East Prussia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Tannenberg).

sides.name: Russian 2nd Army
sides.note: Strength 123,000 (Golovin 1926) to 180,000 (Hastings 2013) per Wikipedia infobox, 612 guns, 384 MGs. infantry_line spans the two figures minus ~20% gunners/support; cavalry = three cavalry divisions, mostly on the flanks and little engaged. Russian 2nd Army was the invader but was encircled; posture 'defend' describes the battle itself. Tech: weapons 6.8 (short of heavy howitzers and shells), logistics 6.3 (railheads ended at the gauge break on the border, troops marched unfed through sand roads), communications 6.5 (orders sent by uncoded radio). Ratings: command 0.3 near 'ad hoc, poor coordination' (Samsonov and Rennenkampf uncoordinated, Zhilinsky remote); morale 0.45 exhausted and hungry after forced marches; training 0.5 conscripts. prepared false: Samsonov's 2nd Army was advancing on the march, its orders broadcast in clear, when it was enveloped (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Tannenberg).

outcome.note: Main battle 26-30 Aug 1914 (5 days); 8 days counting the 23-25 Aug approach fighting. German losses: Sanitaetsbericht 13,873 for 21-30 Aug (1,726 killed, 7,461 wounded, 4,686 missing), Nelipovich ~12,000, West/Elder ~30,000. Russian losses: 70,000 (Russian MoD gwar) to ~120,000 (Nelipovich; 1914-1918-online: 120,000 incl. 95,000 prisoners); high 145,000 = Reichsarchiv 92,000 POW plus ~50,000 killed and wounded, which later Russian work considers inflated. Two corps (XIII, XV) and part of XXIII surrendered; Samsonov committed suicide.

sides.name: French Empire (Napoleon)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. 72,000-73,000: 48,950-50,600 infantry, 14,390-15,765 cavalry, 246-252 guns (Clodfelter, Bodart). Heavy/light cavalry split (cuirassiers, carabiniers, Guard heavy vs lancers, chasseurs, hussars) roughly half each, educated guess. Command 0.7: Napoleon slow to start (ground drying), Ney's unsupported cavalry charges, Grouchy's 33,000 detached. Training 0.7: veteran cadres but a hastily rebuilt army. riverCrossing false: the French attacked across the open valley between the two ridges (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Waterloo).

sides.name: Seventh Coalition (Wellington, Blucher)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. Initial force = Wellington's army ~68,000 (Clodfelter 67,661: 49,608 infantry, 12,408 cavalry, 5,645 artillerymen), 156 guns; heavy/light cavalry split educated guess. Prussians (~48,000 engaged of ~50,000): Bulow's IV Corps attacked Plancenoit at 16:30 (day 0.21 after a ~11:30 start), Zieten's I Corps and part of Pirch's II Corps engaged about 18:00-19:00 (day 0.29). Per-corps split of the Prussian total is an educated guess; 44 guns in action (Clodfelter) to 126 present (Bowden). Training 0.6: British/KGL core, inexperienced Dutch-Belgian, Hanoverian and Landwehr units. Hougoumont and La Haye Sainte were fortified farms (not a fortified city). prepared true for Wellington's army: it reached the Mont-Saint-Jean ridge on the evening of 17 June, deployed on the reverse slope and fortified and garrisoned Hougoumont and Papelotte with La Haye Sainte garrisoned in front; the Prussian contingent arrived on the march (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Waterloo, citing Barbero 2005 p.149).

outcome.note: Coalition victory. French ~25,000 killed or wounded plus 8,000 captured (6,000-7,000 of them wounded), i.e. 26,000-27,000; Barbero 24,000-26,000; high counts captured separately. 15,000 deserted after the battle (not counted). Coalition 24,000: Wellington 17,000, Prussians 6,604-7,000. Start contested (10:00-13:00, ~11:30 usual), ended after 21:00. Rain the night before: muddy ground.

sides.name: Egypt (Second and Third Field Armies)
sides.note: Strength: five infantry divisions each reinforced by an armoured brigade; 'over 100,000 combat troops and 1,020 tanks' crossed 6-9 Oct (Gawrych, Leavenworth Paper 21); Wikipedia: 100,000 soldiers, 1,350 tanks and 2,000 guns and heavy mortars deployed for the assault, 32,000 infantry in the first waves; Egypt total 1,700 tanks, 2,400 APCs, 400 combat aircraft, 140 helicopters, 150 SAM batteries (62 in the front line). Armor high includes the 4th and 21st Armoured Divisions held west of the canal until 14 Oct. infantry_line ~90% of the crossing force, educated; ifv_apc = share of the 2,400 APCs with the two field armies, educated. Air split educated (MiG-21 vs Su-7/MiG-17). Objective: the passes were the stated aim of the 14 Oct offensive; the original plan (Badr) sought only a 10-15 km bridgehead under the SAM umbrella. Tech (derived:tech-anchor, 1973 between 8 and 9): weapons 8.7 (Sagger ATGM, RPG-7, SA-6 guided missiles approach the 1985 anchor); fortification 8.3 (SAM belt, ramparts). Ratings: command 0.55 (excellent crossing staff work, rigid after 9 Oct, 14 Oct offensive outside SAM cover failed); morale 0.8; training 0.55 (drilled for the crossing). Surprise complete (Gawrych). riverCrossing true: the Egyptian offensive opened with an assault crossing of the Suez Canal against the Bar-Lev Line (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Badr_(1973)). objective kind capture: Ismail and Sadat overruled Shazly to seize the Mitla and Gidi Passes and Refidim in the 14 October offensive, which failed (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yom_Kippur_War). Objective point checked 2026-10-30, unchanged: the Mitla Pass is at 30.015 N 32.883 E, about 50 km east of Suez (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitla_Pass). The Egyptian starts are on the canal, the southern (Third Army) one about 37 km west of the pass, and the bridgeheads reached only about 15 km east of the canal by the end of 8 October (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Badr_(1973)), so the pass lay behind Israeli lines at the start.

sides.name: Israel (Southern Command)
sides.note: Start (6 Oct): ~450 men of the Jerusalem Brigade in 16 Bar-Lev forts and 290 tanks in three armoured brigades of the Sinai Division (Wikipedia); infantry high adds the division's mechanised infantry. Reinforcements: day 2 (8 Oct) Adan's 162nd Division (three brigades, 183 tanks + a 44-tank mechanised brigade, Wikipedia) and Sharon's 143rd Division (~200 tanks, educated); day 7-8 further reserves (Magen's division, repaired tanks) bringing the front to 700-750 tanks by 14 Oct (Wikipedia). Artillery and reinforcement infantry are educated guesses. Air: IAF 440 combat aircraft for both fronts; ~half assigned to Sinai, educated split (Mirage/Nesher/F-4 fighters, A-4/F-4 strike). Tech: air 8.8 (F-4E) but heavily attrited by SA-6/SA-2 belt; logistics 8.3 (plus US airlift from 14 Oct). Ratings: command 0.6 (Gonen's failed 8 Oct counterattack, later successful Deversoir crossing); morale 0.8 (existential); training 0.75. Fortified flag false: Bar-Lev forts were too thinly held to act as fortified positions. prepared false: the surprise crossing hit only 450 soldiers in 16 Bar-Lev forts and 290 tanks in all of Sinai, so the Dovecote defence was never manned as planned (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yom_Kippur_War). objective kind capture: Israel's decisive aim was the canal crossing at Deversoir at the northern edge of Great Bitter Lake, through the gap between the Egyptian Second and Third Armies (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yom_Kippur_War).

outcome.note: 6 Oct - first ceasefire 22 Oct (16 days), final halt 24-25 Oct. Winner coded Israel on the military outcome at the ceasefire (Third Army encircled with 30,000-45,000 men, IDF 101 km from Cairo, 1,600 km2 west of the canal) but contested: Egypt held ~1,200 km2 on the east bank and achieved its political aim. Egypt: 5,000-15,000 dead, 8,372 captured (whole war, nearly all Sinai), wounded unknown (educated ~12,000-30,000). Israel: war total 2,521-2,800 killed, 7,250-8,800 wounded, 293 captured (Wikipedia; Gawrych: 2,800+ killed, 7,500 wounded); Sinai share ~two thirds is an educated split (Chinese Farm alone ~300 dead, 1,000 wounded). Grade C on losses.

sides.name: Carthage (Hannibal)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. c. 40,000 or 50,000: 36,000-46,000 infantry in three lines (mercenaries, Carthaginian/Libyan levy, 15,000-20,000 veterans of Italy), 4,000 cavalry (half Numidian), 80+ elephants. Split derived. Mapped to archetype-classical-infantry: weak cavalry, infantry-line battle. Training 0.5: mix of veterans and raw levies. Morale 0.6: new levies wavered. prepared false: both armies deployed in three lines in the open for a pitched battle, Hannibal opening with his elephants (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Zama).

outcome.note: Roman victory. Polybius: Carthaginians 20,000 killed + 20,000 captured; Romans at least 1,500 killed and many wounded. Roman mid 4,000 assumes ~1.5 wounded per killed (derived). Ancient figures, grade C. Exact site of the battle is disputed; coordinates are the commonly cited one.
